thread:
freya-cs: Hey team — Freya (customer) is seeing intermittent API timeouts from the embeddings endpoint since ~02:30 UTC. p95 latency jumps and occasional 401s. Customer says it started after our last region rollout. Logs attached.
support-agent-laura: Thanks, looping in oncall @eng-oncall-jay and infra. Any quick mitigation we can offer the customer? We already applied a temporary rate-limit increase for their account.
eng-oncall-jay: Looking. Do we have exact timestamps and request IDs? Also which region? Can you paste the root request_id from their headers.
freya-cs: RequestIDs: r_0a1b2c3d4e (02:31:12), r_9f8e7d6c5b (02:34:07). Region: eu-west-1. They saw 401s on ~02:34 and timeouts otherwise.
support-agent-laura: Customer repro steps: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"foo"}' https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/embeddings
freya-cs: Also they ran a small local replay (10 qps) and saw p95 go from ~60ms -> 1200ms intermittently.
metrics-bot: quick snapshot: embedding_eu-west1_p95 by minute spiked from 0.06s -> 1.2s at 02:30-02:36 UTC. Underlying host_io_wait increased on a subset of nodes.
eng-oncall-jay: Host IO wait spike suggests storage contention. Did we push the storage driver or CUDA update to eu-west-1 in last 24h? @infra-sam
infra-sam: We rolled cuda-driver-530.12 to a canary pool in eu-west-1 earlier today and promoted to batch nodes at 01:45 UTC. Some hosts also got a firmware microcode patch at 00:50. I'm seeing increased write latency on 3/48 nodes.
sre-olivia: Can someone grab iostat and dstat from a symptomatic host? Suggest checking nvme qdepth and rq_affinity.
infra-sam: iostat snippet from host-evg-12:
```
Device:            tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    await
nvme0n1           942       1200         9800        35.2
nvme1n1           102       1100         10200       28.7
```
That's higher await than baseline (~2-5ms).
eng-oncall-jay: NVMe await spike + CUDA driver rollout matches symptom window. KV cache access patterns for embeddings can amplify host IO noise -> tail latencies. Repro path: run batch of embed requests with small seq len and concurrent KV hits.
support-agent-laura: For customer mitigation, can we route them to a non-canary pool or a fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint? Also increase client retries.
deploy-bot: Rolling traffic route: canary_pool eu-west-1 -> fallback_pool eu-west-1 ready. Command: `route set --from=embed.v1 --to=fallback-embed.v1 --region=eu-west-1 --weight=100` (needs approver)
eng-oncall-jay: +1 to route traffic. Also add short-term server-side retry/backoff: 3 attempts with jitter. I'll push a request-level fallback to smaller kvcache variant.
infra-sam: I'll isolate the 3 nodes and repro with fio. If driver/firmware correlates, we'll rollback the promoted driver on those hosts.
sre-olivia: Ops checklist: (1) Route traffic to fallback pool (2) Isolate nodes and run fio (3) Collect nvme SMART and kernel logs (`dmesg | tail -n 200`) (4) If reproduces, roll driver to previous version in eu-west-1 canary.
billing-ken: Customer impacted — recommend issuing a one-time credit while we investigate. I'll prepare a draft.
support-agent-laura: Noted. I'll tell Freya: temporary routing change to reduce timeouts, we're investigating storage-related root cause, will follow up with timeline. ETA next update in 30m.
freya-cs: Thanks. Customer accepted routing to fallback pool. They're ok with credit if we confirm it's infra.
eng-oncall-jay: Quick config we applied for retries (server-side):
```
retries:
  max_attempts: 3
  base_backoff_ms: 50
  jitter: true
```
This will reduce visible timeouts for now.
infra-sam: fio on host-evg-12 reproduces tail under driver 530.12. Switching back to 528.44 on the node reduces await to baseline.
eng-oncall-jay: Let's schedule a targeted rollback for the 3 impacted nodes and run canary metrics for 15m before broader rollback. @sre-olivia to coordinate.
sre-olivia: Coordinating now. I'll cordon hosts, apply driver rollback, validate embed p95, then uncordon. Will post validation graphs.
metrics-bot: Post-rollback snapshot (after 12m): embed_eu-west1_p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 0.08s on routed traffic; isolated nodes show await drop from 35ms -> 3ms.
support-agent-laura: Customer update: Freya reports errors/timeouts gone after routing, appreciates the quick response. I'll schedule follow-up for status page once we confirm root cause.
billing-ken: Draft credit prepared — 10% for last invoice cycle. Waiting approval.
freya-cs: Customer asked whether this could affect other regions — they run multi-region. Please advise.
eng-oncall-jay: We'll run a quick scan of other regions for any nodes with driver 530.12 and elevated nvme await. If found, apply hotfix or route traffic. Will report back in 45m. :thumbsup:
support-agent-laura: Closing loop: temporary mitigations in place (routing + retries), rollback of impacted nodes started, billing credit pending. Keeping thread open until postmortem.
summary: Customer Freya reported intermittent embeddings API timeouts and 401s tied to p95 spikes in eu-west-1; investigation traced tail latency to NVMe await increase correlated with recent CUDA driver rollout; mitigations: route traffic to fallback pool, server-side retries, rollback drivers on affected hosts, customer credit drafted.
